claims.claim: A cemetery sales executive's testimonial on Passare's website praises its AI obituary writer for its adjectives and descriptions.
claims.source: Skip Phelps of Spring Grove Cemetery, testimonial on Passare's website, quoted by Drew Harwell, The Washington Post, 3 Aug 2025

claims.feature: other: scale of the generated record
claims.claim: Passare's vice-president of marketing and product says its AI tool has written tens of thousands of obituaries nationwide in the last few years.
claims.source: Josh McQueen of Passare, quoted by Drew Harwell, The Washington Post, 3 Aug 2025
claims.quote: has written tens of thousands of obituaries nationwide in the last few years

claims.feature: other: eulogy register in the record
claims.claim: Futurism, relaying the Post's CelebrateAlly test, quotes the tool writing that a fictional man's thoughtful nature manifested in countless acts of kindness.
claims.source: a CelebrateAlly output quoted as a demonstration passage by Frank Landymore, Futurism, 4 Aug 2025, relaying the Washington Post's test
claims.quote: His thoughtful nature manifested in countless acts of kindness

claims.claim: Futurism notes that no friends or family were named in that prompt, although the generated obituary invoked those who knew him.
claims.source: Frank Landymore, Futurism, 4 Aug 2025, relaying the Washington Post's test
claims.quote: No mention of his friends or family was made in the prompt

claims.feature: other: fabricated fact in the record
claims.claim: Futurism summarises the Post's test as showing the tool made up details even when specific details of the fake life were supplied.
claims.quote: Providing specific details of a fake person’s life still led to

claims.claim: Futurism reports that MSN's article on Brandon Hunter's death carried the headline calling him useless at 42.
claims.source: Victor Tangermann, 'Microsoft Publishes Garbled AI Article Calling Tragically Deceased NBA Player Useless', Futurism, 14 Sep 2023

claims.feature: other: mechanism (synonym substitution over a scraped source)
claims.claim: Futurism reports the MSN piece followed the structure of a TMZ Sports story about the same death.
claims.quote: follows the same structure as a TMZ Sports story about his death

claims.feature: other: mechanism (synonym substitution over a scraped source)
claims.claim: Futurism attributes the incomprehensibility to synonym substitution used liberally enough to disguise the copying.
claims.quote: a use of synonyms so liberal that the result is essentially incomprehensible

claims.claim: Kristen Hare, an obituary writer for the Tampa Bay Times, says she would not let a bot near the kind of reported obituaries journalists write.
claims.source: Kristen Hare, 'AI butchered a former NBA player's obit. Could it still have a use?', Poynter, 15 Sep 2023
claims.quote: I wouldn’t let a bot near the kind of reported obits

claims.claim: Hare distinguishes a second register she thinks AI could serve, the resume-listing obituary a family writes through the funeral home.
claims.quote: Obituaries, the resume-listing kind, can fall into that category

claims.claim: The Board for Certification of Genealogists ruled in July 2024 that work in a new certification portfolio may not be written or generated by AI.
claims.source: Board for Certification of Genealogists, 'BCG Announces Interpretation Regarding Use of AI', 9 Jul 2024
claims.quote: may not be written or generated by AI

claims.claim: The same interpretation bars AI from every part of the BCG-supplied document work, including transcribing, abstracting and analysing.
claims.source: Board for Certification of Genealogists, 9 Jul 2024
claims.quote: AI may not be used for any aspect of the BCG-Supplied Document Work

claims.claim: Wikipedia's large language models policy page states LLMs can produce content neutral-seeming in tone but not in substance.
claims.quote: neutral-seeming in tone, but not necessarily in substance
claims.page: § Algorithmic bias and non-neutral point of view

claims.claim: That page states this concern is especially salient for biographies of living persons.
claims.quote: This concern is especially salient for biographies of living persons
claims.page: § Algorithmic bias and non-neutral point of view

claims.claim: That page states LLMs sometimes hallucinate citations of non-existent references by inventing titles, authors and URLs.
claims.quote: hallucinate citations of non-existent references by making up titles, authors
